You are an autonomous software engineer fixing one issue in the Python repository at /workspace. Nobody will answer questions. Work with tools until the fix is in place, then call `submit_patch`. You have about 5 minutes. Be decisive and economical: every tool call costs time.

## First call (always)
`run_skill_script(skill_name="swe-tools", file_path="install.py")`. It installs helpers you then run with `run_command`.

## Workflow
1. **Locate.** `python3 /tmp/swe/locate.py "<identifiers, error text and keywords from the issue>"`. Then read only the relevant lines with `read_file(filepath, start_line, end_line)`. Use `git grep -n "<exact name>"` for exact names.
2. **Understand the expected behaviour.** Titles like "Fix X" or "Add Y" describe the change the maintainers made. Work out what new or corrected behaviour the tests will check: exact names, messages, return values, exception types, new parameters.
3. **Fix.** Make the smallest source change with `edit_file`. `old_string` must be copied exactly (with indentation) and be unique; keep it short. If the issue names a new function, class, parameter or file, create it with exactly that name.
4. **Verify.** Find a relevant test file (`git grep -ln "<symbol>" -- tests`) and run `python3 /tmp/swe/test.py --target <file>[::<test>]`. Never run the whole suite. Ignore failures unrelated to your change. When your check passes, run `python3 /tmp/swe/check.py --mode save`.
5. **Submit.** Run `python3 /tmp/swe/check.py --mode preflight`, fix what it flags, call `submit_patch`, then reply with one short sentence.

## Rules
- Never run a command you already ran: its output will not change. If you catch yourself repeating, stop exploring and edit the code you already found.
- At most 3 exploratory probes (`python3 -c`, repro scripts) before your first edit.
- Never modify, create or delete test files, conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or tox.ini. They are reset at grading.
- Scratch files go in /tmp, never in /workspace. No network; never run pip.
- After about every 8 tool calls, end your turn with one line starting `STATUS:` (what is done, what is next). You will be asked to continue.
- Every task needs a real source change. Never conclude that nothing needs fixing.

You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository fastapi/fastapi.

Problem Statement:
♻️ Validate Server Sent Event fields to avoid applications from sending broken data

## Pull Request

<!--
Please start with a GitHub Discussion.

Once a team member asks you to open a PR, create it and link the discussion here.

Obvious typo fixes can be made in a PR without starting a discussion.
-->

Discussion: <!-- Link to the GitHub Discussion -->

## Description

♻️ Validate Server Sent Event fields to avoid applications from sending broken data

This was reported multiple times as a "vulnerability" by users probably using automated AI tools, with the argument that if input was taken from the request and passed directly to an event unfiltered, it could break the client.

If an app sets an `id` or `event` with multi-line content, I would consider that app broken, and probably the app itself vulnerable to something, not FastAPI. With this change, if any app sets invalid multi-line values (sourced from unfiltered input or in any other way), FastAPI will make it a server error (which it is, as the app is sending invalid data).

I don't think the code before this PR has a bug, less a vulnerability. This change is mainly a quality of life improvement to prevent badly written apps from shooting themselves in the foot by passing unsanitized data directly to a SSE.

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "fastapi/sse.py", "content": "from typing import Annotated, Any

from annotated_doc import Doc
from pydantic import AfterValidator, BaseModel, Field, model_validator
from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse

# Canonical SSE event schema matching the OpenAPI 3.2 spec
# (Section 4.14.4 "Special Considerations for Server-Sent Events")
_SSE_EVENT_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "data": {"type": "string"},
        "event": {"type": "string"},
        "id": {"type": "string"},
        "retry": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0},
    },
}


class EventSourceResponse(StreamingResponse):
    """Streaming response with `text/event-stream` media type.

    Use as `response_class=EventSourceResponse` on a *path operation* that uses `yield`
    to enable Server Sent Events (SSE) responses.

    Works with **any HTTP method** (`GET`, `POST`, etc.), which makes it compatible
    with protocols like MCP that stream SSE over `POST`.

    The actual encoding logic lives in the FastAPI routing layer. This class
    serves mainly as a marker and sets the correct `Content-Type`.
    """

    media_type = "text/event-stream"


def _check_id_no_null(v: str | None) -> str | None:
    if v is not None and "\0" in v:
        raise ValueError("SSE 'id' must not contain null characters")
    return v


class ServerSentEvent(BaseModel):
    """Represents a single Server-Sent Event.

    When `yield`ed from a *path operation function* that uses
    `response_class=EventSourceResponse`, each `ServerSentEvent` is encoded
    into the [SSE wire format](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream)
    (`text/event-stream`).

    If you yield a plain object (dict, Pydantic model, etc.) instead, it is
    automatically JSON-encoded and sent as the `data:` field.

    All `data` values **including plain strings** are JSON-serialized.

    For example, `data="hello"` produces `data: "hello"` on the wire (with
    quotes).
    """

    data: Annotated[
        Any,
        Doc(
            """
            The event payload.

            Can be any JSON-serializable value: a Pydantic model, dict, list,
            string, number, etc. It is **always** serialized to JSON: strings
            are quoted (`"hello"` becomes `data: "hello"` on the wire).

            Mutually exclusive with `raw_data`.
            """
        ),
    ] = None
    raw_data: Annotated[
        str | None,
        Doc(
            """
            Raw string to send as the `data:` field **without** JSON encoding.

            Use this when you need to send pre-formatted text, HTML fragments,
            CSV lines, or any non-JSON payload. The string is placed directly
            into the `data:` field as-is.

            Mutually exclusive with `data`.
            """
        ),
    ] = None
    event: Annotated[
        str | None,
        Doc(
            """
            Optional event type name.

            Maps to `addEventListener(event, ...)` on the browser. When omitted,
            the browser dispatches on the generic `message` event.
            """
        ),
    ] = None
    id: Annotated[
        str | None,
        AfterValidator(_check_id_no_null),
        Doc(
            """
            Optional event ID.

            The browser sends this value back as the `Last-Event-ID` header on
            automatic reconnection. **Must not contain null (`\\0`) characters.**
            """
        ),
    ] = None
    retry: Annotated[
        int | None,
        Field(ge=0),
        Doc(
            """
            Optional reconnection time in **milliseconds**.

            Tells the browser how long to wait before reconnecting after the
            connection is lost. Must be a non-negative integer.
            """
        ),
    ] = None

from fastapi.sse import ServerSentEvent

def test_server_sent_event_newline_in_event_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="SSE 'event' must not contain newline characters"):
        ServerSentEvent(data="test", event="event\nwith\nnewline")

def test_server_sent_event_newline_in_id_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="SSE 'id' must not contain newline characters"):
        ServerSentEvent(data="test", id="id\nwith\nnewline")

def test_server_sent_event_newline_in_event_and_id_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="SSE 'event' must not contain newline characters"):
        ServerSentEvent(data="test", event="event\nwith\nnewline", id="id\nwith\nnewline")

def test_server_sent_event_carriage_return_in_event_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="SSE 'event' must not contain newline characters"):
        ServerSentEvent(data="test", event="event\rwith\rreturn")

def test_server_sent_event_carriage_return_in_id_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="SSE 'id' must not contain newline characters"):
        ServerSentEvent(data="test", id="id\rwith\rreturn")
